# NOTES (sga3): Companies Act 1967 (Singapore), ss 76B to 78K, lines 8312 to 9881 of `inputs/CoA1967.txt`

**Status, 2026-11-18.** This file is generated by `work/gennotes.py` (not shipped) from the seven layer-1 modules, the raw text and the hand-written readings; every name, count, line number and quotation below was read from a file by that script, and the script stops when a fork tag has no register entry (or the reverse), a subsection has no jural row, a "may" function has no gate class, a unit has no locator, or a regulative rule's breach path disagrees with its traces.
What it says about layer 1: the 193 `@ref` blocks declare 193 functions and rules and 20 types; the tests hold 674 assertions and 46 `#TRACE`s; the seat holds 74 questions and 169 case assertions.
The section "Tests, seat and what check.sh prints" says what was run and what it printed.
Nothing here says a reading is right: it says what the code does and which words of the text it relies on.

**Layers.** Layer 1 (`sga3-76b.l4`, `sga3-76c-76e.l4`, `sga3-76f-76g.l4`, `sga3-76h-76k.l4`, `sga3-77-78.l4`, `sga3-78a-78c.l4`, `sga3-78d-78k.l4`) is the law, objectively; `sga3-tests-*.l4` are its tests; layer 2 is `sga3-seat.l4` (questions an individual asks) and `sga3-cases-seat.l4` (its cases).

**BRIEF.md and PLAN.md.** The brief governs where it differs from `inputs/PLAN.md`.
I found no point where they conflict on a name or a seam; the brief states requirements the plan does not (the coverage table, the `JUST FALSE` and `NOTHING` rule and its two marginal readings, the grant rule of 2026-11-12, the two split sites, a `BREACH` trace for each regulative rule, the comparison with the earlier pass), and those were applied as the brief states them.
Where PLAN.md section 6 lists keel names for this part, the encoding calls the keel functions listed in "Seams" and asks the others (`"treasury share"`, `"share"`, `"voting share"`, `"listed"`, `"constitution"`, `"book-entry securities"`) as plain facts named for the fact.

**Source quotes.** Every rule cites the text with `-- src:N | text` lines and an `@ref LABEL (src:A-B)` locator, copied by script from the raw file; `srcrefs.py check` and `--strict` report 0 problems, and `work/checkquotes.py` finds every quoted fragment of a `-kind` comment in the text.


## Edition encoded

The Companies Act 1967 (Singapore), 2020 Revised Edition, as rendered by the Singapore Statutes Online (SSO) informal consolidation "version in force from 6/5/2026 to 20/10/2026", retrieved 2026-10-09 (`inputs/SOURCES.md`), which carries the amendments up to Act 24 of 2025.
A later consolidation may exist; none was read.
The file is a PDF turned into plain text by a converter script: a rendering, not the official text, and nothing in this folder is claimed to be verified against the official text.
The rendering has artefacts (page furniture inside the text, an arrangement of sections at the head that this encoding did not use, and in s 76D(4A) a stray line `(b) as the case may be.` that is the tail of paragraph (b)); amendment marks such as `[36/2014]` are not text.


## Coverage (sga3)

One row per section, subsection, paragraph, subparagraph, marginal heading, Division heading and defined term of lines 8312 to 9881, built by `work/coverage.py` from the text itself and joined to the `@ref` locators of layer 1 by line overlap (a row is covered when its own lines, up to its first child, overlap a locator).
A row has exactly one disposition: `encoded`, `fork` (the rule that encodes the row carries at least one fork-register entry; the entries are named in the last column and the readings are in the register), `inert` (reason 1 only: the marginal headings, the Division heading, the page furniture and the amendment marks; there is no row with reason 2 or 3) or `repealed or blank in this text`.
A section row whose text is its subsections is `encoded` by the rows below it.

## Fork register (sga3)

Every fork tag in layer 1 (`{F-..}` in a comment, or `fork F-..` in a comment line) has one entry here, and every entry has a tag: 90 entries (the script stops otherwise).
The last column quotes the words of the text that license the reading taken, read from the `-kind` comment of the function that carries the tag (a few entries carry a quotation written here from the text: F-A7, F-A10, F-B3, F-G1, F-I3, F-P1, F-78K1).
"Other reading" says what the answer would be if the text were read the other way.
The brief's rule on the grant ruling is applied as it states it (limit 1: `NOTHING` for a function named for a grant whose "if" gate failed, one fork line each; limit 2: `JUST FALSE` where the text closes the gate itself or for a bar, a duty or the provision's own question; limit 3: the "where", "when", "upon" group and the "entitled" group are listed, not decided).
The rulings that govern the `NOTHING-kind` tags in this folder are recorded again here, word for word, as the Guide gives them (lines 86 to 99 of `inputs/ENCODING-GUIDE.md`; lines 88 to 90 are the Guide's own preamble and are left out):


> Guide line 86: In short, a function answers `JUST FALSE` only where the text itself says no to the case in its own words: a "means" definition, a condition the text introduces with "if", "only if", "as long as" or "unless" (and plain variants such as "while", "until" and "except"), a list the text closes with "only", a flat negative ("does not", "shall not", "may not").
> Guide line 87: Everywhere else it answers `NOTHING`: where the text lists without closing the list, says "includes", leaves a term undefined, is silent, points outside the sources, or limits a grant or prohibition in its own wording and the case falls outside the limit.
> Guide line 91: - **E1** (bench `commons-negation-1030`; should a legal effect be one definition gathered from every section that gives it?): option B, as guidance for gathering a legal effect's routes by hand only, with no pilot run; option A (gathering by bare name) is withdrawn as a direction for the language, not deferred; option C (per-section answers) applies everywhere else; the Magna Carta pilot in the printed recommendation (chapters 2, 3, 4, 5, 37, 43, 46 and 53, with a blind second reader) is not to be run. The maintainer's lean, verbatim: "B but generally uncomfortable with this much magic because it takes the language from unopinionated to opinionated in ways that are hard to teach an l4 novice." the maintainer's note, verbatim: "Fundamentally I feel like we are trying to make the language do work that the human l4 drafter should do. Too much magic. Can’t we just decline to be this opinionated and say the programmer needs to do this thinking?" Marked 2026-11-03T23:19:02.812Z, ruled 2026-11-04. Bench: https://claude.ai/artifact/49q6k2H5xtuJqy5ttkwZ23
> Guide line 92: - **N2** (bench `commons-negation-1030`; does a flat negative count as the text's no?): option A as printed: flat negatives count as a no, and where the text names the bearer the prohibition (`SHANT`) is derived from that answer; the Hohfeld kinds stay in each row's "Jural relations" table; option C's wording (the kind typed in the person-facing answer) comes only after a lawyer confirms the typing, decided together with the S/E choice for how "not covered" is said. The maintainer's lean, verbatim: "Why are we even trying to do this work? > Guide line 93: - **Periods, "where" and scope limits** (a question raised on 2026-11-05 while checking an encoding of the Retirement and Re-employment Act 1993, not a bench): (a) a period the text fixes in its own words ("within one month", "begins from ... until the employee attains the age", "on the last day of employment"): outside the period the answer is `JUST FALSE`; (b) a "where ..." condition: when it fails the answer is `JUST FALSE`; (c) a scope limit with no "only" (for example "below" the minimum age): outside the scope the answer is `NOTHING`. The maintainer's words, verbatim apart from the trigger word that ended the message: "i agree with your lean: no for a and b; nothing for c." Typed 2026-11-05T04:30:00.322Z, ruled 2026-11-05.
> Guide line 94: - **Delegated definitions, defences and "until" bars** (questions raised on 2026-11-05 while checking encodings of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002, the Terrorism Act 2000 and the Singapore Sale of Goods Act 1979, not a bench): (a) a definition the text itself hands to a list ("Schedule 9 has effect for determining what is a business in the regulated sector"): when no head in the list holds, the answer is `JUST FALSE`; a bare list with no such hand-off still answers `NOTHING`; (b) "it is a defence ... to prove that X": when X is not proved, the answer is `JUST FALSE` for that provision's defence, worded "this section gives no defence on these facts" and never "no defence at all"; (c) "when", "upon" and "whenever" count as "where" under rule (b) of the periods ruling above; (d) "the property does not pass until X": encode the bar ("the property cannot yet pass": `JUST TRUE` before X, `JUST FALSE` after X) and never claim that the property has passed. The maintainer approved these four readings as put to him by the general-manager session, in the word NOTHINGBURGER; his note on (d), verbatim apart from the bracket and the trigger word that ended the message: "in the case of Q5 [the "until" bar] i hope we are using the deontic mechanisms to examine a trace." The note is a request about how (d) is modelled, not part of the ruling. Typed 2026-11-05T06:04:54.553Z, ruled 2026-11-05.
> Guide line 95: - **Questions with no convention: decide case by case (the maintainer, typed 2026-11-05T10:25:24Z).** Six questions the rulings above leave open are decided site by site, at encoding time, on the text's own words and the encoder's best judgment: an "unless" or "except" once it is met; a bare "must" not done; "listed in Schedule N"; a duty whose "if" or "where" is unmet; "(other than X)"; a missing event in the state ledger. Each such site gets one fork line (the provision, the function, the answer taken, the other reading) for the human reviewer to overrule, and the rulings above still govern whatever they cover. The maintainer's words, asked of the session "Encodings": "re Encoding Conventions I believe I had a short discussion with the coordinator where I basically said I agreed with its \"lean\"s -- does that mean we can retire the bench card or should I go over it still? In short I feel like these decisions need to be made case-by-case at encoding time, and you should go with your gut most of the time; and if the encoding turns out to be wrong, well, that's where the human review comes in." The bench that carried the six questions ("Encoding Conventions", artifact Hpg2k9HqExJN5zdtBYiJ72, collection `encodings-conventions-1105`) was retired unmarked, so it holds no marks.
> Guide line 96: - **Functions named for a grant or a power (ruled by the coordinating session of the UK and Canada encodings on 2026-11-12; not confirmed by the maintainer).** A function named for a grant or a power ("the court may ...", "the registrar may ...") that answers `JUST FALSE` because an `if` gate failed reads as "may not": a grant turned into a bar. The ruling sets three limits:
> Guide line 97: 1. answer `NOTHING`, with one fork line each, only for a function named for a grant or a power ("may", "is permitted to", "has power to") whose `if` gate failed;
> Guide line 98: 2. keep `JUST FALSE` where the text closes the gate itself ("only if", "only where", "may not ... unless", a list closed with "only"), and for a bar, a duty or the provision's own question;
> Guide line 99: 3. do not change, but list in the row's fork register for the maintainer or a lawyer, a "may" function whose gate is "where", "when" or "upon" (ruling (b) of the periods ruling above says `JUST FALSE`, and the "In short" line on grants points the other way), and an "entitled"-named function (an entitlement is a claim, not a power, and this guide does not settle it).

### Grant-named functions: inventory and counts (grant ruling of 2026-11-12)

The grant rule of 2026-11-12 is recorded in the Guide as "ruled by the coordinating session of the UK and Canada encodings on 2026-11-12; not confirmed by the maintainer".
Functions whose name carries "may": 35 (two of them, in s 78, are a number and a date and not grants).
Of these, 7 answer `NOTHING` because an "if" gate failed (limit 1; each has its fork line above), 5 answer `JUST FALSE` because the text closes the gate itself (limit 2: "only if", "if, and only if", "may only", "so long as") or because a fixed period is missed (periods ruling item (a)), and the rest answer `NOTHING` because the text names no gate, lists without closing, or limits itself by a named complement.
The "where", "when", "upon", "on application" and period group (limit 3) has 6 sites and 7 functions, marked "split site (ii)" below; they are listed without a ruling and the answer is whatever the Guide's own rulings and the wording gave (see "Split sites").
Functions named "entitled": 0; no function of this range carries the word (the one place the text says "entitled", s 78D(3), is a status of the creditor and the function is named `subsection (2) applies to the creditor`).

## Jural relations (sga3)

One row per subsection (and per unnumbered paragraph of s 78, and per section for ss 78J and 78K, which have no subsections), covering the whole range.
The "kind" column uses Hohfeld's pairs: right/duty (claim), privilege/no-right, power/liability, immunity/disability.
Where the text names the bearer of a prohibition, the `SHANT` rule is derived from the flat negative (ruling N2, option A); the kinds are written here and are not typed into the answers (option C waits for a lawyer).
A provision that creates no relation (a definition, a counting rule, a scope rule, a repealed text) is listed once as `none`.
The "L4 rule(s)" column names the functions whose locator overlaps the rows of the provision (at most four are shown).
The holders and bearers are stated in the words of the text's own actors (the company, the directors, the Court, the Registrar, creditors, members); where the text names no actor, the table says who benefits as the claim-holder.

## Marginal readings for a lawyer (sga3)

Two readings are flagged "for a lawyer, not for you to decide" in the brief; every branch below rests on one of them.
**MR-a.** A failed "if" counts as the text's no, clause by clause, within the provision that holds the "if" (an inference: "if A then B" does not itself say "if not A then not B"), and flat negatives count as the text saying no.
Other reading of MR-a: the failed "if" (or the flat negative) is not the text saying no to the case, so the branch answers `NOTHING`.
**MR-b.** A prohibition or grant limited by its own wording does not count as the text's no: the case outside the limit answers `NOTHING`.
Other reading of MR-b: the case outside the limit is the text's no and answers `JUST FALSE` (for a grant, "may not").
Rule: every `FALSE-kind` branch that is not a "means" definition carries `{MR-a}` and every `NOTHING-kind (limited by its own wording)` branch carries `{MR-b}` in the comment of layer 1; the script stops when one lacks its tag.
The "means" definitions (eight: "relevant period", "equal access scheme", "associated person", "contingent purchase contract", "cash", "reduction information" and the two "qualifying creditor" branches) are the text's own no in the Guide's list ("a \"means\" definition") and carry no marginal tag.
102 MR-a branches and 86 MR-b branches follow, in text order, with the words of the text.
The fork entry (last column) states the other reading of a specific site; where it is blank the other reading is the one stated here.

### Reading a result: FALSE and NOTHING (sga3)

A function answers `MAYBE BOOLEAN` (or `MAYBE NUMBER`, `MAYBE DATE`): `JUST TRUE` is yes, `JUST FALSE` is the text saying no in its own words (a `-- FALSE-kind` comment quotes the words), and `NOTHING` is "the text does not say" (a `-- NOTHING-kind` comment says why: silent, list not closed, includes, undefined term, points outside the text, limited by its own wording).
A caller must never turn `NOTHING` into `FALSE`; in particular the seam `s 7(9)(ca)` (see "Seams") asks a `BOOLEAN` of a `MAYBE BOOLEAN` answer.

How the common shapes read:
- **An "until" bar** (`s 76B(8)`, `s 76K(1B)`, `s 78G(1) ... cannot yet take effect`, `s 78E`'s "take effect when"): `JUST TRUE` before the event and `JUST FALSE` after it (the ruling of 2026-11-05, item (d)); the code never claims that the thing "has taken effect".
- **An offence function** (`s 76F(3)`, `ss 78B(5)`, `78C(5)`, `78F(5)`, `78H(5)`, `78J`): `JUST FALSE` means this subsection makes the person guilty of nothing on these facts; it does not say the person is innocent of any other offence.
- **A penalty record** (`s 76F(3) penalty`, `s 78H(5) penalty`): the amounts are copied from the text; `NOTHING` where the person is not the one the subsection makes guilty; the field "the court may impose both" is `JUST FALSE` because the text says "or" and not "or to both".
- **A grant named "may"** whose "if" gate failed answers `NOTHING`, not `JUST FALSE`: `JUST FALSE` would read as "may not".
- **A duty** whose requirement is not met (the provision's own question, "has the company obtained the consent the subsection requires") answers `JUST FALSE`; where the duty's "Where" is unmet the answer is a site-by-site call (see F-D4 and F-78E2).
- **A counted period** is worked out only by the keel's `period:` functions; a period "beginning with" or "ending with" a named day counts that day as day 1 and calls the keel with the count less one (F-P1).

**A seam the plan lacks (the type).** The keel's `sg-interests` asks the fact `the interest is a company's interest in its own shares purchased or otherwise acquired in accordance with sections 76B to 76G (including treasury shares)` as a plain `BOOLEAN`, and this part answers a `MAYBE BOOLEAN`: `JUST TRUE` when the power, the scope, the 20% limit and the authority hold, and `NOTHING` otherwise, because the sections never say what an acquisition that fails one of their conditions is called (fork F-B11).
Wiring `NOTHING` to `FALSE` would turn "not covered" into "no" at the seam, which the rule of 2026-10-29 forbids; the lead has to choose how a `NOTHING` is carried into a `BOOLEAN` (and the keel's name ends "(including treasury shares)" while this part's function name does not, because none of the sections' conditions turns on treasury holding).
After the independent review the function answers `JUST FALSE`, not `NOTHING`, when a condition fails, and a second function, `s 76B(1) the keel's s 7(9)(ca) field: the interest is in accordance with sections 76B to 76G`, turns it into the `BOOLEAN` the keel asks (assumed, not ruled; see the top-level `NOTES.md`, section "Changes made after the independent review").

**Answers of this part that other functions of this part take as facts.** `the purchase or acquisition has been authorised as section 76C, 76D, 76DA or 76E requires` (used by `s 76B(1) the interest ...`) is answered by the `s 76C(2)`, `s 76D(2)`, `s 76DA(1)` and `s 76E(1)` functions; the caller combines them, and this part does not (the sections do not say how).

**Facts the text hands to the Minister, the Court, the Registrar or a prescribed form** are plain inputs named for the fact (never guessed): the 20% in `s 76B(3)` ("or such other percentage as the Minister may by notification prescribe"), the other purpose of `s 76K(1)(e)`, the other rate of `s 78(d)`, the publicity requirements of `ss 78B(1)(c)`, `78C(1)(c)`, the further period `s 76I(3)` lets the Registrar allow and the longer period `s 78I(3)` lets the Registrar allow, and the prescribed forms and fees.

## Split sites (sga3)

The brief records two questions the Guide leaves open, site by site; this section counts the sites and gives the answer taken at each, with the fork line (the entry in the fork register) and the line of `inputs/ENCODING-GUIDE.md` the answer relies on, quoted.
Nothing was changed to match what another part might have done.
**(i)** An unmet element of an offence or a contravention: `JUST FALSE` or `NOTHING`?
**(ii)** A "may" gated by "where", "when", "upon", "on application", a stated period or a condition word: `JUST FALSE` (periods ruling, rule (b)) or `NOTHING` (the grant ruling)?

**Counts.**
- Site (i), offences: 6 sites, all `JUST FALSE` (the subsection's own question; F-F5, F-A8 for two subsections, F-78F2, F-78H3, F-78J1).
- Site (i), contraventions: 5 sites, all `JUST FALSE` (F-A5, F-78F4).
- Site (i), bars with an unmet element: 5 sites: the two ceilings of s 76I are `JUST FALSE` when their "Where" fails (periods ruling item (b); F-I2), and the three prohibitions of ss 76E(1), 76J(4) and 76K(3) are `NOTHING` outside their own wording (the "In short" sentence; F-E1, F-J1, F-K5).
- Site (ii): 6 sites in 7 functions: `JUST FALSE` at 2 sites (s 76F(1), s 78D(2)), `NOTHING` at 4 sites (s 76H(1) with two functions, s 76K(1), s 76K(1C), s 78I(1)).
Every site that rests on a reading the Guide does not settle is also listed under "Marginal readings for a lawyer" (MR-a for the `JUST FALSE` answers, MR-b for the `NOTHING` answers).
The `NOTHING` answers at site (ii) are the ones most likely to be overruled: the periods ruling's item (b) and rule (c) say a failed "where", "when" or "upon" is `JUST FALSE`, and this encoding answers `NOTHING` for a "may" because the grant ruling says a grant turned into a bar reads as "may not"; the other reading at each is in the register.


## Rules with no breach path (sga3)

6 of the 19 regulative rules in this range have no breach path, because the text gives no deadline and no consequence: a `MUST` with no `WITHIN` and no `LEST` can never reach `BREACH`, and a late act still reads `FULFILLED`.
The text does not say when "as soon as possible" ends (s 78D(4)), and says nothing of what follows a failure to make the solvency statement available at the meeting (ss 78B(4)(a), 78C(4)(a)), to reduce capital (s 76G(1)) or for the Court to ascertain the names (s 78H(4)(a)); no deadline or consequence was invented.
For each there are a `FULFILLED` trace (the act happens) and a `RESIDUAL` trace (nothing happens in the window), as the Guide's trap says ("A `SHANT` traced with no events reads as a standing obligation (`RESIDUAL`), which is not a pass").
The other 13 rules each have a trace that reaches `BREACH`, and every trace carries an `-- EXPECT` comment that was compared with the output on build 110 and on build 109.

## Compared with the earlier pass

The earlier pass (`inputs/NAIVE-EVIDENCE/`) covers ss 76B(1), (3), (5), (7), (8), 76D(2), (2A), (3), (4), (4A), (7) and 76F(1) to (4) (its own header says so) and encodes them as plain `BOOLEAN`s.
Nothing was copied from it: not its names, not its code and not its expected values; its case facts were reused where noted.
Where this encoding reads a provision differently, the fork register has the entry; the cases that differ are these (my answer was run on the earlier pass's facts with `l4 run`, build 110, in a throw-away file that was removed; the earlier pass's answer is read from its source and its cases file).

| provision | the earlier pass's case | the earlier pass answers | this encoding answers | why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| s 76B(1) | the same buy-back without a permission in the constitution | `BOOLEAN` false (not authorised) | `NOTHING` for `s 76B(1) the company may purchase or otherwise acquire shares issued by it` | a grant named "may" whose "if" gate failed (F-B1; grant rule, limit 1); the other reading is the earlier pass's |
| s 76B(3) | buying back 21 of 100 shares after a section 78B reduction | within the limit (a reduction in the relevant period lifts the limit) | `s 76B(3) the number purchased ... exceeds the limit` for 21 of 100 at 20%: `JUST TRUE` (exceeds) | reading A of F-B3: subsection (3A) says "despite subsection (3)(a) and (b)", so the limit still bites after a reduction and is measured on the altered total |
| s 76D(2A) | the shares are all the shares in their class | consent is satisfied (`TRUE`) | `NOTHING` | the subsection says "Where ... do not constitute all the shares in that class, the company must ... obtain the consent"; where that is not so it says nothing (F-D4; the other reading is `JUST FALSE` by the periods ruling item (b), which is a marginal reading) |
| s 76D(2A) | only Haziq's class consent (50% of the other holders) | not authorised | `JUST FALSE` for the consent function (4 holders, 2 consented) | the same answer on the same facts; "75% of the holders" is counted by heads in both passes (the text says "holders", F-D3) |

| s 76F(2)(a) | lawful, with the company solvent | `TRUE` | `NOTHING` for `s 76F(2)(a) ... is lawful` when solvent | the text says only that "no purchase ... is lawful" when the conditions are not met (a flat negative, `JUST FALSE`); it does not say the purchase is lawful when they are met |

Cases where the two agree on the value (and differ only in the wrapper): s 76F(4) solvency (both `FALSE` or `JUST FALSE` when a condition fails, both `TRUE` when all hold, both with the "intended winding up" fork in (b)); s 76F(3) amounts (both $100,000 and 3 years); s 76F(3) "or" and not "or to both" (the earlier pass notes it, this encoding carries it in the penalty record).
The earlier pass leaves out ss 76B(3A) to (3E), (4), (5A), (6), (9), (10), 76C, 76DA, 76E, 76G to 76K, 77, 78 and 78A to 78K; the comparison stops at what it covers.


## What the text turns out to say

1. **A six-month period that begins on a month-end.** `s 76I(3)`: "before the end of the period of 6 months beginning with the day on which that contravention occurs" counts the day named as day 1, so the period ends the day before the same date six months on; the keel steps months by clamping to the last day of a short month, so for 31 August 2026 stepping 6 months gives 28 February 2027 and "less one day" gives 27 February 2027, which is wrong by a day.
The code tests the round trip (stepping the clamped date back 6 months returns the start day) and takes minus one day only if it does, otherwise the clamped date itself (`sga3-76h-76k.l4:131`; test `sga3-tests-76h-76k.l4:39`: 31 August 2026 ends on 28 February 2027).
NEEDS-CORE.md asks the keel for the function.
2. **The 20% limit survives a reduction of capital.** `s 76B(3)(a)` and `(b)` say "unless" and then "the company has, at any time during the relevant period, reduced its share capital", and `s 76B(3A)` then says, "despite subsection (3)(a) and (b)", the total is the altered total; read together the limit still bites after a reduction, measured against the altered total (F-B3, reading A); the test of the altered total is at `sga3-tests-76b.l4:35` (a reduction: the limit is measured against 800 and not 1000).
3. **Four parallel consent subsections that do not run in parallel.** `s 76D(2A)`, `(5A)` and `(9A)` exclude the sellers and their associated persons from the holders whose 75% consent is needed; `(12A)` does not (F-D3); "holders" is counted by heads in all four.
4. **"Or" is not "or to both".** `s 76F(3)` gives "a fine not exceeding $100,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 3 years"; the penalty record carries `the court may impose both` as `JUST FALSE`; `s 78H(5)` is worded the same way.
5. **The six weeks and the eight weeks.** "The 6 weeks beginning with the resolution date" are days 0 to 41 after the resolution date; a creditor may apply on any of them and not on day 42 (the day-42 assertion is at `sga3-tests-78d-78k.l4:17`), and the documents of `s 78E(1)(d)` are lodged "after the end of 6 weeks, and before the end of 8 weeks, beginning with the resolution date", that is on days 42 to 55 (`sga3-78d-78k.l4:94`).
6. **A failed "Where" in a duty is answered two ways.** `s 76D(2A)`, `(5A)`, `(9A)`, `(12A)` answer `NOTHING` when the "Where" fails (F-D4, the Guide's open question about "a duty whose `if` or `where` is unmet"), while `s 78E(1)` to `(4)`, `s 78F(4)` and `s 78I(3)` answer `JUST FALSE` by the periods ruling item (b) (F-78E2, F-78F4, F-78I2).
The questions differ (`has the company obtained the consent the subsection requires` against `has the company lodged what the subsection requires for the reduction to take effect`), but the shape is the same and a lawyer may want one answer for both.
7. **"Throughout the 6 weeks" is a duty and a prohibition.** `s 78B(4)(b)` and `s 78C(4)(b)` cannot be one "within": the statement must be available from day 0 and must not be withdrawn up to day 41; the rule is a `MUST` at day 0 with `HENCE` a `SHANT` to withdraw until day 41 (F-A10); the trace whose withdrawal is at `sga3-tests-78a-78c.l4:127` reaches `BREACH` when the statement is withdrawn on day 20, and the trace at `sga3-tests-78a-78c.l4:121` is `FULFILLED` when it is there on day 0 and nothing is withdrawn up to day 42.
8. **A unit with no function until the coverage table asked.** `s 78F(1)` ("An application by a creditor under section 78D is to be determined by the Court in accordance with this section") had no function; the coverage script found it (see Coverage), and it now has one with two assertions at `sga3-tests-78d-78k.l4:90`.
9. **The rendering.** In `s 76D(4A)` the line `(b) as the case may be.` is the tail of paragraph (b), not a paragraph; the coverage script treats a repeated label as such.
10. **The text does not answer** (the sections state a condition and not its consequence): what an acquisition that fails one condition of ss 76B to 76G is called (F-B11); what follows a failure to make the solvency statement available at the meeting (s 78B(4)(a), s 78C(4)(a)); how long "as soon as possible" is (s 78D(4)); when the Registrar's "further period" under s 76I(3) or s 78I(3) ends (an input); whether the 75% of holders in s 76D(2A) is by heads or by shares (counted by heads, F-D3).


## What the stable binary does not accept

Met while writing (probed on build 1.6.110 on 2026-11-18, or hit in a first draft):
- `MAX` does not exist (`check/unknown-identifier`); the code writes the `IF ... THEN ... ELSE` that picks the larger.
- In a `#TRACE`, `WAIT UNTIL 10` is an error (`check/unknown-identifier`, `check/not-a-function`); the event is spelled `WAITUNTIL`; a party argument needs parentheses (`(Director "D One")`).
- A regulative rule names a constructor of an `IS ONE OF` act type; a trace must spell the constructor exactly as the type declares it (for `s 76G act` that includes the words `, or both,`).
Taken from PLAN.md section 5 and followed, not re-probed here: `#ASSERT` on one line, every `NOT` parenthesised, `DECIDE name IF` takes a `BOOLEAN` (a `MAYBE BOOLEAN` result is a `GIVETH`/`MEANS` pair), `YMD` (write `Date day month year`), `REFUSE`, `#ASSERT REFUSED`, `BECAUSE` outside `LEST BREACH ... BECAUSE`, `TYPICALLY` on a field, sets and `EVERY`, section-level `GIVEN`, and `AFTER` in a deontic window are not available on the stable binary; a name defined in two imported modules cannot be used at all (every name here begins with its section label for that reason).
The silent traps the plan lists (`NOT a AND b`, `Date 29 2 2023` rolling forward, `add months` clamping, a `MUST` with no deadline never reaching `BREACH`) were each met by a test or a rule in this range: the clamping in finding 1, the missing breach path in "Rules with no breach path".


## Tests, seat and what check.sh prints

Tests: 674 assertions in `sga3-tests-*.l4` (87, 160, 38, 87, 48, 104, 150 in the order of the modules), each expected value written from the text before the run; 46 `#TRACE`s, each with an `-- EXPECT` comment, compared with the output on builds 110 and 109; the seat `sga3-seat.l4` has 74 questions and `sga3-cases-seat.l4` 169 assertions.
The seat (layer 2, `sga3-seat.l4`) asks each question as "Under section N, ..." in the Act's own numbering, for an individual who is or will be a director, a company secretary or a member, or who deals with a company; every question takes plain inputs with an `@desc`, builds the records layer 1 expects inside the question and calls the layer-1 rule, so no rule is restated; the regulative rules are not exported (their deadline is asked as "what is the last day ..."), and there is no seat for the Registrar, the Minister or the Court.
Both seat files are generated by scripts in `work/` (not shipped) from the layer-1 signatures and a hand-written specification; the generated files are not edited by hand.
A mutation spot-check changed eight single places in layer 1, one at a time, and ran the matching test file on build 110: the comparator of `s 76B(3)`, the 30 days of `s 76B(9)` into 31, the 89 days of `s 78I(3)` into 90, the 19 days of `s 78C(3)(b)` into 20, the "both" flag of the `s 76F(3)` penalty, the 75% comparator of `s 76D(2A)`, an answer of `s 76J(3)`, and the 55 days of `s 78E(1)(d)` into 56.
Seven were killed by the first test run; the eighth, `s 78I(3)` 89 into 90, survived until two boundary assertions were added (29 September and 28 September 2026 against an order made on 1 July), and then failed as it should.
The throw-away files were removed.

Baseline and result: the eight keel modules (`sg-*.l4`) print 0 assertions in the table below, so the run before this part's files existed totalled 8 modules and 0 assertions satisfied; it now totals 24 modules and 843 assertions satisfied, 674 in the test files and 169 in the seat cases, with 0 errors, 0 failed and 0 refused on build 1.6.110 and the same four counts on the main build 1.6.109 for every module.
The exit status was 0.
`L4_MAIN` was set to the 1.6.109 binary (so `fetch-main-l4.sh` was not run) and `JL4_LIBRARY_PATH` was unset.

## The S1b ruling on failed gates (2026S1bC)

The Guide records this ruling at section 5, in the bullet that begins “Failed gates of the pure “may” functions”; it is copied here word for word, as the Guide asks of every ruling.

> - **Failed gates of the pure "may" functions of the two Singapore encodings: the split follows the background, not the holder's name (card S1b of the bench "Singapore Split Sites", option C as modified on the card; accepted by Meng).** Conditions as printed on the card: (1) It governs only the functions that stay Boolean after the protocol split, the pure gates (58 on the card's line); the type (i) sites, an unmet element of an offence, are unchanged. (2) A failed gate answers `JUST FALSE` where the function is a public body's power, a relief from an express bar or duty, or a gate the text closes (“so long as”, “only if”); it answers `NOTHING` where it states a company's or person's liberty, standard or privilege with no bar to relieve. (3) At the card's reading that changes 16 answers: 6 `NOTHING` to `JUST FALSE` at public bodies, and 10 `JUST FALSE` to `NOTHING` at liberties (C024, C046, C084, C115, C135, C138, C154, C155, C157, C159), each a fork line with the other reading and each borderline, because a relief and a liberty are a judgment. The 10 liberties that already answered `NOTHING` stay. (4) Applied one commit per part, each “assumed, not ruled” until the card was marked, flipping the branch each site's tag marks. (5) The difference between an express bar and silence stays in the code's `FALSE-kind` and `NOTHING-kind` comments and in NOTES, which is the provenance channel, and not in the truth value. (6) Recorded in this guide, with limit 3 of the grant ruling above replaced for the Singapore rows, and in the `NOTES.md` of the parts that carry limit 3 (the card's own wording; this paragraph is that record). (7) The ruling reaches the two Singapore encodings only. The UK (164 listed sites) and Israel stay on the Guide as it stands until Meng rules; until then the differential compares Singapore under C with the UK under limit 3. The sites the 16 answers belong to: the public-body powers that went from `NOTHING` to `JUST FALSE` are s 173F (C045), s 32(4) (C106), s 139(6) (F018), s 139(10) (F019), s 282AA(1) (F057), s 281(1) (F062); the liberties that went from `JUST FALSE` to `NOTHING` are s 145(1), s 202A(2), s 21(7), s 130(2), s 173J(3), s 179(2), s 387A(1), s 387B(1), s 387D, s 390(1). Meng's note, verbatim: “Suggest that the changed encodings, and future rules encoded under this ruling, be marked with a greppable string like 2026S1bC to show where this rule took effect. Then in future we can revisit and review the consequences of this rule on encodings that haven’t been done today.” Marked 2026-11-21T12:17:37.989Z (accept, option C, not blind), ruled 2026-11-21, so the commits that applied it are ruled and no longer “assumed, not ruled”. Reading of the note (assumed, not ruled): each function this ruling changed, and each function encoded later under it in these two encodings, carries the string `2026S1bC` in its `FALSE-kind` or `NOTHING-kind` comment, and on its `FORK` line where it has one, so that `grep -rn 2026S1bC` lists where the rule took effect and a later review can find its consequences. Bench: https://claude.ai/artifact/SYSny5zjFYHHcMFeNYi5RX

No site of this part changed under it (2026S1bC): the functions of this part that stay Boolean after the protocol split already answered as the ruling reads, and its protocol-shaped functions keep limit 3 of the grant ruling until they are re-encoded.
